husk.name: Coir Fiber
husk.imageAlt: Natural coconut coir plant pots on wooden surface
husk.description: The fibrous outer layer that shields the coconut fruit contains resilient, naturally lignin-rich fibers. Once extracted without harsh chemicals, it provides the structural backbone for biodegradable vessels and nursery pots.
husk.gain: Direct replacement for single-use polypropylene plastic nursery containers.

pith.name: Organic Cocopeat
pith.imageAlt: Rich organic cocopeat growing medium with seedlings
pith.description: Between the long fibers lies a spongy cellular dust that holds water like a sponge. Washed and prepared with care, it serves as a peat-free growing medium.
pith.p1: Absorbs up to 8x dry weight in water
pith.gain: Helps protect peat bog ecosystems and reduce irrigation frequency.

shell.name: Bio-Carbon & Polished Shell
shell.imageAlt: Coconut shell charcoal briquettes beside polished shell
shell.description: The hard shell protecting the coconut meat contains high carbon density. Processed carefully, it produces long-burning briquettes; hand-carved, it becomes lasting tabletop ware.
shell.p2: Low ash content and odorless combustion
shell.p3: Polished with pure virgin coconut oil
shell.gain: Reduces open-air agricultural burning and wood-based charcoal use.

home.metaTitle: NIRA | Value Beyond Waste · Circular Coconut Materials
home.metaDescription: Discover the NIRA circular ecosystem: coconut husks, residue, and shells become living vessels, organic growing media, clean energy, and heirloom homeware while supporting local communities.

hero.callout: BECAUSE EVERY NATURAL POSSIBILITY NEEDS ROOM TO BEGIN.
hero.description: NIRA is an Indonesian circular ecosystem that transforms overlooked coconut biomass into plant pots, organic growing media, clean energy, and functional craft with local communities.
hero.note: We make room for the potential of coconut and skilled hands through meaningful circular products.
hero.imageAlt: Whole coconut, split shell, coir fibers, and green sprout arranged together

story.title: See what others leave behind.
story.p1: After a coconut is consumed for its water and food, its rough outer husk, fine spongy pith, and hard dense shell can still have immense regenerative purpose. Across tropical coastlines, these valuable components are all too often burned as waste or abandoned.
story.p2: NIRA begins with a different conviction: what could each material become when met with care and craft? The answer connects thoughtful mechanical processing with functional everyday products and new economic dignity for farming communities.
story.imageAlt: Naturally harvested coconut husks and shells drying on woven bamboo mats
story.imageNote: Harvested coconut husks drying under tropical sunlight in East Java, Indonesia.

materialsIntro.title: A whole story in every part.
materialsIntro.description: Explore how each anatomical component of the coconut takes a distinct regenerative path, engineered by nature and refined by human hands.

journey.title: Every step carries value forward.
journey.description: A circular idea becomes meaningful through rigorous material science, respect for natural architecture, and fair human participation at every stage.

collect.title: Collect
collect.subtitle: Ethical Sourcing
collect.summary: Collect unused husks and shells with local farmers.
collect.text: Partnering directly with smallholder farming communities to collect post-harvest husks and shells that were previously discarded or burned.

process.title: Process
process.subtitle: Zero-Chemical Refining
process.summary: Separate fiber and pith with natural methods.
process.text: Separating long tensile fibers from spongy peat pith using rainwater washing, sun-curing, and mechanical decortication.

create.title: Create
create.subtitle: Artisan Formulation
create.summary: Shape fibers, cocopeat, and shells into useful products.
create.text: Molding breathable coir vessels, screening nutrient-holding cocopeat, and carbonizing dense shells into clean burning briquettes.

empower.title: Empower
empower.subtitle: Circular Prosperity
empower.summary: Support village workshops and future research.
empower.text: Reinvesting revenue directly into village processing hubs, safe artisanal workshops, and continuous regenerative research.

impact.title: Impact across three dimensions.
impact.description: NIRA measures success through regenerative loops, fair household stability, and measurable ecological renewal.

community.caption: Pak Wayan Sudarma, Lead Artisan Coordinator in Banyuwangi, East Java.
community.title: Change is made by hands.
community.quote: At NIRA, the coconut husks and shells we once burned or discarded now provide new income while helping keep our soil and sea clean.
community.description: From gathering raw husks to precision coir decortication and hand-finishing bowls, NIRA centers the ecological knowledge of coastal agricultural communities. Every vessel sold supports family incomes.
community.imageAlt: Pak Wayan smiling in a sunlit coconut craft workshop

cta.title: What could we reveal together?
cta.description: Whether you are a horticultural brand seeking peat-free circular substrates, an architectural studio exploring bio-composites, or a sustainability advocate, we welcome thoughtful collaborations that keep nature and community at the center.
